messages.author: 9ec69ca07f36d6a1
messages.subject: Parameterized macros (template)
parts:
In using the nice facility provided by knit_expand there is a nice advantage of using global variables, e.g.,

<<{{prefix}}-mychunk>>=

where prefix is not given in the knit_expand call but was defined earlier in the knitr document.

But it would be beneficial to also have parameterized macros so that the user could completely list the macro
variables so that the code could tell when they are not present, and to provide defaults.  For example:

% In template.Rnw to be called by knit_expand
% knit_expand var1,var2,print=FALSE (or some standard markup)
A \LaTeX\ sentence ....
<<{{prefix}}-mychunk>>=
plot({{var1}}, {{var2}})
if({{print}}) {
  print(var1)
  if(mvarthere({{var2}})) print(var2)  # if var2 is not given don't let it revert to a previous definition outside the invocation 
@

(e.g. mvarthere <- function(x) !missing(x))

The invocation could be knit_expand('template.Rnw', var1=age, var2=cholesterol) or
knit_expand("template.Rnw", var1=age, var2=cholesterol, print=TRUE)

Do you think this would be possible?

Thanks for considering,
Frank

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Parameterized macros (template)
parts:
Perhaps you mean something like this?

mvarthere <- function(x) exists(deparse(substitute(x)),
envir=parent.frame(), inherits = FALSE)

The key is inherits=FALSE, which stops R from looking for objects in
parent frames successively.

Regards,
Yihui
--

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Parameterized macros (template)
parts:
"Default values" are a feature of functions, so you can wrap a
function around knit_expand() to achieve this goal, e.g.

library(knitr)
f = function(x, y = 2, ...) {
knit_expand(text = "x is {{if (missing(x)) 'unknown' else x}}, and
y+1 is {{y+1}}", ...)
}

> f()
[1] "x is unknown, and y+1 is 3"
> f(x = 'foo')
[1] "x is foo, and y+1 is 3"

I'm not sure if this answers your question.

Regards,
Yihui
--

messages.author: 9ec69ca07f36d6a1
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Parameterized macros (template)
parts:
I think it does.  What is the most elegant way to have extended inline text defined inside a function, with preserved or specified newlines?  E.g.

f <- function(x, y=2, ...) {
w <- "
<<mychunk,echo=TRUE,cap='A caption'>>=
z <- 'this'
plot(runif(20))
@
"
knit_expand(text=w)
}

One thing that always causes confusion is having to use alternate quote marks ' or "" or to escape quotes with \' \" when using this approach.

Frank

This approach also avoids confusion between having to quote or escape text.

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Parameterized macros (template)
parts:
I think in this particular situation inheriting from the global environment might be undesirable, since the OP wants to explicitly pass parameters to the macro.

However, I do agree that there might be times when you want to be able to use everything in your global environment. My guess is it is more useful in interactive situations, where you dont want to worry about being explicit. But in other situations, being explicit encourages reproducibility.
